v1.certificate_notes: copy_assign.rs and collapse_gate.rs share the certificate literally: collapse_gate.rs imports and calls copy_assign::poisson_binomial_upper_tail directly, and both apply the same alpha=1e-3 Bonferroni form (copy_assign.rs uses `p.alpha / n.saturating_sub(1).max(1)`; collapse_gate.rs compares `p_value >= alpha`, alpha=GENOME_WIDE_EPS_AMB=0.001313 by default in its own test, 1e-3 elsewhere). absent_copy.rs does not call poisson_binomial_upper_tail; it calls min_p_distinct (defined in copy_split.rs, imported into absent_copy.rs), which its own doc-comment states is 'the same construction the assignment gate uses, copy_assign.rs:320': a product-of-per-base-error-rate certificate compared against the same alpha threshold, i.e. the same significance FORM (Pi(error/3) over distinguishing columns, < alpha => certifiably distinct) but a distinct function, not a shared call. Recorded as genuinely shared in form/parameterization across all three files; copy_assign.rs and collapse_gate.rs additionally share the literal function call.

READ_CAP.code_path: src/rustle/vg_family/o2_materialize.rs:250 fetch_reads() -- caps the per-FAMILY multimapper read-sequence pool `seqs` (unique read NAMES, first-seen across all of a family's PAD=2000bp-padded copy regions, primary+secondary alignments both counted, unmapped/supplementary excluded, `de` tag required). This is the gw_family_catalog / bench/o2_vg_visualization.py code path, NOT the copy_assign binary -- copy_assign uses its own reads_in_region/pass1_skeletons and has no READ_CAP.
READ_CAP.measurement_method: direct samtools count (not a copy_assign run, since copy_assign does not call fetch_reads): for GWFAM42 (the Soto family with the highest avg_reads = 876.8, 6 copies on chr2), `samtools view -F 0x804 <region+-2000bp>` per copy region, read names deduplicated across all 6 regions.
READ_CAP.family: GWFAM42 (chr2, 6 copies, avg_reads=876.8, the highest-avg_reads of the 66 Soto families)
READ_CAP.observed_max_basis: unique read names across GWFAM42's 6 PAD-padded copy regions combined (family-wide pool, as fetch_reads accumulates it)

observed_single_locus.region: chr2:87767940-87796331 (highest single-copy read count in the 66-family set; +/-2000bp pad used for the count below)

READ_CAP.note: Compile-time const; not toggled (no rebuild -- out of scope here, deferred to deliverable B). Real BAM data (A119b.t2t.bam, gorilla IsoSeq on CHM13v2.0, -N50 multimapping) shows the observed family-wide pool (22454) is 3.7x over the 6000 cap, and even a SINGLE locus alone (20564 incl. secondary) already exceeds it without combining copies. Confirms READ_CAP's existing heuristics.toml tier="result-guard" is correct.

POA_CAP.code_path: src/rustle/vg_family/copy_assign_pipeline.rs:524 -- gates the poasta (exact O(n^2)) vs minimap2-MSA engine choice by the LONGER of two copies' genomic span length in bp (`ref_span.len().max(spans[other].len())`).
POA_CAP.measurement_method: direct max(end-start) over every copy row in bench/soto/a119b_detected_copies.tsv (66 families, all copies).
POA_CAP.note: Compile-time const; not toggled (no rebuild -- deferred to deliverable B). Direct measurement over all 66 Soto families' copies shows the longest copy span (260931 bp) is 13x over the 20000bp cap, so real Soto-scale copy pairs are routed to the minimap2-MSA fallback instead of poasta. Confirms POA_CAP's existing heuristics.toml tier="result-guard" is correct.

copy_assign_baseline.purpose: sanity/reference run on the same locus used for the READ_CAP single-locus measurement -- not itself a POA_CAP toggle (that region's family detection found 0 homology edges, so no POA comparison ran there; the POA_CAP evidence above comes from the direct table measurement instead).
